content: Rifampin and isoniazid are indicated for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis caused by susceptible organisms. This fixed-dose combination should only be used after the patient has been titrated on the individual components, confirming that the fixed dosage is therapeutically effective. The recommended dose is rifampin 600 mg and isoniazid 300 mg (two capsules) taken orally once daily. This combination is not recommended for initial therapy of tuberculosis or for preventive therapy. Safety and efficacy in patients under 15 years of age have not been established. Rifampin significantly decreases the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of several drugs by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of rifampin with these drugs is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced efficacy, loss of therapeutic effect, or development of resistance. Below are specific interactions: 1. Artemether/lumefantrine: Rifampin reduces their levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to decreased antimalarial efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Atazanavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing antiviral efficacy and potentially leading to viral resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Bictegravir: Rifampin decreases its plasma concentration via CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 induction, risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Cabotegravir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing systemic exposure and risking virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Cariprazine: Rifampin reduces its levels by inducing CYP3A4, affecting the formation and elimination of active metabolites. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Cobicistat: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Cobimetinib: Rifampin reduces its systemic exposure by over 80%, significantly decreasing efficacy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Darunavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing antiviral efficacy and risking resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Doravirine: Rifampin reduces its plasma concentration, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Elbasvir/grazoprevir: Rifampin reduces their therapeutic effect via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: Rifampin reduces their levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Etravirine: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing its levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin increases its metabolism, reducing antiviral efficacy and risking resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Fostemsavir: Rifampin significantly decreases its active moiety (temsavir) plasma concentrations, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir: Rifampin significantly reduces their plasma concentrations and AUC, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Irinotecan: Rifampin reduces its levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: Rifampin reduces sofosbuvir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein, decreasing its active metabolite. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Lenacapavir: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Lonafarnib: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Lorlatinib: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor: Rifampin reduces ivacaftor exposure by 57%, risking reduced efficacy. Co-administration is not recommended. 23. Lurasidone: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Mavacamten: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Naloxegol: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is not recommended. 26. Nelfinavir: Rifampin reduces its plasma concentrations, risking therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir: Rifampin reduces nirmatrelvir levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir: Rifampin reduces their levels, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Panobinostat: Rifampin reduces its levels by ~70%, risking treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Pirfenidone: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP1A2 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Praziquantel: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Regorafenib: Rifampin reduces its levels and increases exposure to its active metabolite. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Rilpivirine: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Roflumilast: Rifampin reduces its systemic exposure, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is not recommended. 35. Tipranavir: Rifampin reduces its levels, risking antiviral failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Vandetanib: Rifampin reduces its exposure by up to 40%, risking therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Velpatasvir: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP2B6 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Voriconazole: Rifampin reduces its levels by increasing metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Abemaciclib: Rifampin reduces its plasma concentration. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 40. Abrocitinib: Rifampin reduces its levels via CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 induction. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 41. Acalabrutinib: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 42. Adagrasib: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 43. Afatinib: Rifampin reduces its levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 44. Almotriptan: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 45. Alpelisib: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 46. Alprazolam: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 47. Amiodarone: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 48. Apixaban: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 49. Apremilast: Rifampin reduces its systemic exposure. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 50. Aprepitant: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 51. Aripiprazole: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 52. Atorvastatin: Rifampin reduces its levels and increases toxicity risk. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 53. Avapritinib: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. 54. Axitinib: Rifampin reduces its levels. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug used. In summary, rifampin interacts with numerous drugs by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, leading to reduced plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy. Co-administration with these drugs is often contraindicated or requires careful consideration of alternative therapies.
